news.title: Top performers at European track and field championships to each get 50,000 euro bonus
news.description: Ten track-and-field athletes with the best performances at next week's European championships will each receive a bonus of 50,000 euros ($58,000), the continent's governing body for athletics has confirmed. European Athletics said its “gold crown initiative,” launched at the 2024 edition in Rome, will reward athletes across five groups of events in Birmingham for both men and women. A bonus — and gold crown — will go to the athlete in each group of events who “achieves the highest scoring performance in their respective finals using World Athletics scoring tables,” European Athletics said.

snippets: The highest paid athlete in the world as of May 2026 was Cristiano Ronaldo. The Al-Nassr soccer star took home total earnings of 300 million U.S. dollars, of which an estimated 65 million U.S. dollars were off-field earnings through endorsements. Despite the ongoing debate among fans and in the media about who is the better soccer player between Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, it is the former that led the way in terms of total earnings in 2025/26.

One notable absence in the list of highest paid athletes is any female athletes. In fact, the highest paid female athletes took home a fraction of the earnings of their male counterparts. Tennis star Coco Gauff topped the list of sportswomen, having taken home eight million U.S. dollars in prize money and a further 23 million U.S. dollars in endorsements in 2025. Gauff consistently ranks in the top 10 of the WTA's ranking of female tennis players worldwide, and her endorsements include companies such as New Balance, Bose, and Rolex.
